title: Rationalization of point-section transformations with normalized scalar equation
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$. All coefficient fields below are finite intermediate extensions of $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$, with valuation rings and uniformizers [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and let $g:s\to s$ be a scheme automorphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], put $\mathcal C_E^{\rm int}=D^b_c(s,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], $\mathcal C_E=D^b_c(s,E)$, the raw rationalization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], and $P_E=Lg_E^*$ with its specified integral, rational and common-stage actions [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Let $F_E^{\rm int}=\Gamma(s,-)$ and $F_E=\operatorname{Fib}_s:\mathcal C_E\to D^b_{\rm fd}(E)$ be the specified point-section functors [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], and put $H_E=F_EP_E$.

For integral scalar extension $U_{L/E}$ [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], let $\alpha_K:U_{L/E}P_EK\xrightarrow{\sim}P_LU_{L/E}K$ and $\varphi_K:F_L^{\rm int}U_{L/E}K\xrightarrow{\sim}F_E^{\rm int}K\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L$ be the specified comparisons [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension, lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension]. Suppose that $\eta^E:F_E^{\rm int}\Rightarrow F_E^{\rm int}P_E$ is any natural transformation for each $E$ and that
$$\varphi_{P_EK}F_L^{\rm int}(\alpha_K)^{-1}\eta^L_{U_{L/E}K}=(\eta^E_K\otimes1)\varphi_K$$
for all inclusions and all $K$, with the given unit and tower identifications.

For $E\subseteq L$, write $S_{L/E}K=K\otimes_E L$ for rational scalar extension and $T_{L/E}A=A\otimes_E L$ on point complexes [def-weil-point-fd-qlbar-category]. Let $\bar\alpha_{E,L,K}:S_{L/E}P_EK\xrightarrow{\sim}P_LS_{L/E}K$ and $\bar\varphi_{E,L,K}:F_LS_{L/E}K\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{L/E}F_EK$ be precisely the rationalizations of the specified completed pullback and sections comparisons [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension, lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension]. Define
$$b_{E,L,K}=\bar\varphi_{E,L,P_EK}\circ F_L(\bar\alpha_{E,L,K}^{-1}):H_LS_{L/E}K\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{L/E}H_EK.$$

The maps $t_{E,K}=\eta^E_K\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$ have source $F_EK$ and target $H_EK$ in $D^b_{\rm fd}(E)$ and form natural transformations $t_E:F_E\Rightarrow H_E$ on the entire raw rational category. In particular, for every integral $v:K\to K'$, $a\in E$, and every finite sum $u=\sum_jv_j\otimes a_j$, the specified morphism actions and naturality satisfy
$$F_E(v\otimes a)=a(F_E^{\rm int}(v)\otimes E),\quad H_E(v\otimes a)=a(F_E^{\rm int}(P_Ev)\otimes E),\quad H_E(u)t_{E,K}=t_{E,K'}F_E(u).$$
These equations hold for the balanced tensor classes, including zero and torsion integral objects, with no injectivity hypothesis on localization of Hom groups. For every $E\subseteq L$ the normalized rational scalar equation is
$$b_{E,L,K}t_{L,S_{L/E}K}=(t_{E,K}\otimes_E L)\bar\varphi_{E,L,K}.$$
Here the comparisons, including their inverses, are the rationalizations of exactly the supplied integral comparisons, and their identity and successive-extension equations remain valid after rationalization.

For the literal Lean realization use the canonical small coefficient model $\operatorname{Shrink}(E)$ and the inclusions conjugated by its specified algebra equivalence with $E$, as in [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. All finite-field families and comparison equations use these same models; the common-stage target retains the prescribed transports back to the actual subfields. The duplicated rational and common-stage helper definitions are aliases of the canonical constructions in [lem-weil-point-rational-family-common-stage-naturality]; this concerns only its definitions, not that theorem as a proof assumption.

source.place: Deligne, Weil II, (1.1.3), p. 150; (1.1.7), pp. 150-151 gives the point-transport context only. Original coefficient-descent proof steps 1-3: raw morphism tensors and rationalization of the normalized integral equation. The completed pro-etale normalization and explicit formulas are an agent-written argument, not assertions attributed to Deligne.

proof.text: Put $R=\mathcal O_E$ and write $q_E(N)=N\otimes_R E$ on module complexes, with the linear arrow action of [def-weil-module-base-change]. This is a functor on derived categories by [lem-weil-coefficient-complex-rationalization]. By [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], $F_EK=q_E(F_E^{\rm int}K)$, so $t_{E,K}=q_E(\eta^E_K)$ has exactly the required endpoints. The morphism formula of that definition and the rational pullback formula of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] give the two displayed pure-tensor actions. For $r\in R$ their balancing is explicit: $a\,q_E(F_E^{\rm int}(rv))=a\,q_E(rF_E^{\rm int}(v))=(ra)\,q_E(F_E^{\rm int}(v))$, and likewise after $P_E$. Thus the formulas respect $(rv)\otimes a=v\otimes ra$, addition in each factor, and the zero relations. They act on tensor classes, not on chosen fraction presentations.

source.place: (1.1.3), p. 150, scalar extension of Hom groups; (1.1.7), pp. 150-151, point-transport context only. The explicit balanced-tensor and comparison argument here is written by Q10, not asserted by Deligne.

proof.text: Integral naturality gives $F_E^{\rm int}(P_Ev)\eta^E_K=\eta^E_{K'}F_E^{\rm int}(v)$. Apply the functor $q_E$, multiply by $a$, and use the bilinearity of composition in the $E$-linear derived category [lem-weil-linear-abelian-derived-category, def-weil-linear-category]. Using Step 1, this is $H_E(v\otimes a)t_{E,K}=t_{E,K'}F_E(v\otimes a)$. By [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], every rational arrow is a finite sum of such tensors. Add the equations and distribute composition over addition to obtain the asserted equation for $u=\sum_jv_j\otimes a_j$. Since Step 1 supplies maps on the balanced tensor product, this equality is independent of the sum representing $u$.

source.place: (1.1.3), p. 150, scalar extension of Hom groups; (1.1.7), pp. 150-151, point-transport context only. The explicit balanced-tensor and comparison argument here is written by Q10, not asserted by Deligne.

proof.text: No cancellation of the map from integral Hom groups has occurred. For example, if $\varpi_E^n v=0$, then $v\otimes a=(\varpi_E^n v)\otimes(\varpi_E^{-n}a)=0$, and the balanced actions of Step 1 send this class to zero. If $\varpi_E^n\operatorname{id}_K=0$ then the same calculation makes $\operatorname{id}_K\otimes1=0$, so the localized object and its images under the specified functors are zero objects. More generally any integral object whose rationalization is zero has zero identity there, and functors preserve that identity and zero. The preceding equations therefore also apply to zero objects and torsion objects, without assuming any integral Hom map injective.

source.place: (1.1.3), p. 150, scalar extension of Hom groups; (1.1.7), pp. 150-151, point-transport context only. The explicit balanced-tensor and comparison argument here is written by Q10, not asserted by Deligne.

proof.text: Fix $E\subseteq L$ and apply $q_L=-\otimes_{\mathcal O_L}L$ to the assumed integral scalar equation. Use the natural isomorphism $\beta_{L/E,N}$ of [lem-weil-coefficient-complex-rationalization] to identify $q_L(N\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L)$ with $q_E(N)\otimes_E L$. Its naturality for derived arrows identifies $q_L(\eta^E_K\otimes1)$ with $t_{E,K}\otimes_E L$. The left comparison factors become precisely $\bar\varphi_{E,L,P_EK}$ and $F_L(\bar\alpha_{E,L,K}^{-1})$: these are the stipulated rationalizations, and $F_L$ acts on the integral arrow $\alpha_K^{-1}$ by $q_LF_L^{\rm int}$ from Step 1. The remaining factors become $t_{L,S_{L/E}K}$ and $\bar\varphi_{E,L,K}$. Thus the tensored equality reads $\bar\varphi_{E,L,P_EK}F_L(\bar\alpha_{E,L,K}^{-1})t_{L,S_{L/E}K}=(t_{E,K}\otimes_E L)\bar\varphi_{E,L,K}$, exactly the normalized equation with the defined $b$.

source.place: (1.1.3), p. 150, scalar extension of Hom groups; (1.1.7), pp. 150-151, point-transport context only. The explicit balanced-tensor and comparison argument here is written by Q10, not asserted by Deligne.

proof.text: The comparisons in [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension] and [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension] are natural isomorphisms with the stated unit and successive-extension compatibilities. Applying $q_L$ preserves a comparison and its specified inverse: the equations $cc^{-1}=1$ and $c^{-1}c=1$ become the same equations for their images. Naturality after rationalization follows by multiplying the image of each integral naturality square by a scalar and adding, as in Step 2. Apply the same tensor functors to the supplied unit and tower equalities. For the module-complex identifications, the identity and tower clauses of [lem-weil-coefficient-complex-rationalization] identify the resulting diagrams with the stipulated rational diagrams. Thus all these equalities remain valid for the actual supplied comparisons, including $L=E$; no replacement of the comparisons or their inverses is made.

Step 2: apply q_E to integral naturality, then use bilinearity of composition in D(E) and that every raw rational arrow is a finite sum of pure tensors (def-weil-rationalization-karoubi). This gives exactly b t_L = (t_E⊗L) φ̄, with the correct orientation. Step 5: the inverses, naturality, and unit and tower equations pass through the functor q, using β's unit and three-field clauses. Small cases checked: L=E, K=0, torsion K, and the empty sum. No cycle: the item is not in its own dependency closure of 11385 nodes. No SGA.
